notes: Night 1 surfaced a methodology problem before any business insight: Grace's agent-group report rolled up every tenant's same-named group (e.g. all 120 merchants' 'Customer Care') into one row, while Omar's SLA-breach-by-group report kept each tenant's group separate (171 rows). The two reports use different grains under the same label, so they can't be compared, and neither tells us whether load/staffing is balanced within a real operational unit (a tenant's own group). Also, the company briefing says a handful of merchants drive most volume — I haven't checked that at all yet, and Daniel explicitly asked to flag any single merchant driving disproportionate pain. So tonight I'm fixing the grain: first, ticket volume and SLA performance by merchant to find concentration and any outlier tenant; second, the highest-volume tenant+group combinations (the real staffing units) to redo the staffing-balance read properly; third, a day-of-week/time-of-day cut of SLA breaches since Daniel specifically asked about time patterns and I have a slot free for it. Headline SLA numbers from report 3 (37.7% first-response breach, 20.3% resolution breach, urgent tickets breaching resolution over half the time) are worth noting to Mia/Daniel now even before drill-down.

requests.title: Ticket volume and SLA performance by merchant
requests.question: Is ticket volume and SLA breach pain concentrated in a handful of merchants, and do any merchants stand out as outliers?
columns: agent_count (distinct support_agents belonging to that tenant via agent_group_members, or via support_agents.tenant_id if simpler)
requests.details: Window: tickets.created_at between 2025-01-01 and 2025-12-31. Source tables: tickets (join tenants for name), sla_breaches (breach_kind = first_response / resolution, as % of that tenant's tickets with sla_policy_id not null), support_agents. Order by ticket_count descending; print the top 30 rows but note the total number of tenants with at least one ticket in 2025. Round rates to 1 decimal percent, cumulative_pct to 1 decimal.
builds_on: Ticket volume and staffing by agent group
SLA breach rates by agent group

requests.title: Highest-volume merchant + agent-group units
requests.question: At the real operational unit (one merchant's one agent group), where is ticket load heaviest, and does staffing (agent count) look right for that load?
columns: agent_count (support_agents in that tenant's group via agent_group_members)
requests.details: Window: tickets.created_at between 2025-01-01 and 2025-12-31, tickets.agent_group_id not null. Source tables: tickets, agent_groups, agent_group_members, support_agents, tenants, sla_breaches. Group by tenant_id + agent_group_id (do not roll up by group name across tenants). Order by ticket_count descending, show the top 20 rows, and note how many (tenant, agent_group) combinations exist in total in 2025. Round tickets_per_agent to 1 decimal, rates to 1 decimal percent.
builds_on: Ticket volume and staffing by agent group
SLA breach rates by agent group

requests.title: SLA breach rates by day of week and time of day
requests.question: Is there a time-of-day or day-of-week pattern to when we breach first-response and resolution SLA targets?
requests.grain: one row per combination of ticket creation day-of-week (Monday..Sunday) and time-of-day bucket (Night 00-06, Morning 06-12, Afternoon 12-18, Evening 18-24, all in UTC)
requests.details: Window: tickets.created_at between 2025-01-01 and 2025-12-31, restricted to tickets with sla_policy_id not null. Derive day-of-week from tickets.created_at (use calendar_days.day_name joined on the date, or extract directly) and a 6-hour UTC time bucket from the created_at time component. Source tables: tickets, sla_breaches, calendar_days. 28 rows total (7 days x 4 buckets); order by day_of_week (Monday first) then time_of_day_bucket in chronological order (Night, Morning, Afternoon, Evening). Round rates to 1 decimal percent, minutes to whole numbers.
builds_on: SLA breach rates by priority, with overall headline rate
